title: Diatom communities in Antarctic green macroalgae
author: Juliana Ferreira da Silva
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6tcheiw

steps.title: Collect and freeze algal samples
steps.instruction: Collect ~100 g portions of Prasiola crispa at each sampling point, place each portion in a labelled zip‑bag and freeze the bags for later processing.

steps.title: Optional immediate microscopy
steps.instruction: If possible, take a small aliquot of the fresh sample and observe it under an optical microscope immediately after sampling to record the community before oxidation.

steps.title: Oxidize organic material
steps.instruction: Treat the frozen algal material with hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) and potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) for one week, replacing the H₂O₂ solution daily and heating the samples during the week to improve oxidation.

substeps.instruction: Add sufficient H₂O₂ and KMnO₄ to cover the material.
Incubate for 7 days, changing the H₂O₂ solution each day.
Apply gentle heating (temperature not specified) throughout the incubation.

steps.title: Wash oxidised material
steps.instruction: Rinse the oxidised samples thoroughly with distilled water to remove residual chemicals.

steps.title: Mount permanent slides
steps.instruction: Mount the cleaned material on permanent microscope slides using Naphrax mounting medium (refractive index 1.74; Brunel Microscopes Ltd, Chippenham, UK).

steps.title: Light‑microscopy analysis
steps.instruction: Examine the permanent slides under a Leica DM750 microscope with a 100 × objective for qualitative and quantitative observations.

steps.title: Prepare samples for SEM
steps.instruction: Filter selected material through a polycarbonate membrane filter (pore size 3 µm), then mount the filter pieces on SEM stubs.

steps.title: Platinum sputter coating
steps.instruction: Coat the mounted filters with platinum using a BAL‑TEC MED 020 Modular High‑Vacuum Coating System for 30 seconds at 100 mA.

steps.title: SEM imaging
steps.instruction: Image the coated samples with a Hitachi SU‑70 scanning electron microscope (Hitachi High‑Technologies, Tokyo, Japan) operating at 5 kV and a working distance of 10 mm.

steps.title: Count diatom valves
steps.instruction: Count approximately 80 diatom valves per sample across the necessary number of permanent slides; identify each taxon using the appropriate Antarctic diatom bibliography.

steps.title: Calculate geographic distances
steps.instruction: Using the recorded latitude and longitude of each sampling site, compute pair‑wise Euclidean distances (in metres) and assemble a geographic distance matrix.

steps.title: Build biological similarity matrices
steps.instruction: Create two matrices for the samples: (1) relative abundance matrix (individuals per taxon) and (2) species‑composition matrix (presence/absence of taxa).

steps.title: Estimate species richness
steps.instruction: Estimate total species richness by simple arithmetic of the chosen estimators (without standard deviations) and calculate sample sufficiency as the percentage of observed values relative to the estimated total.

steps.title: Generate rarefaction curves
steps.instruction: Construct individual rarefaction curves for each sampling point, standardising to the lowest sample size (N = 41) to correct for differences in effort.

steps.title: Run EstimateS randomisations
steps.instruction: Perform the rarefaction analysis in the EstimateS program with 100 randomisations of the abundance data (Colwell 2013).

steps.title: Create rank‑abundance diagrams
steps.instruction: Plot rank‑abundance diagrams for each site using relative abundance data and compute the Pielou equitability index (based on the Shannon diversity index).

steps.title: Partition diversity with Hill numbers
steps.instruction: Partition diversity into alpha, beta and gamma components using Hill’s numbers via the ‘entropart’ R package (multiplicative partitioning).

steps.title: Compute Jaccard and Bray‑Curtis dissimilarities
steps.instruction: Calculate Jaccard (incidence) and Bray‑Curtis (abundance) dissimilarity matrices for all pairs of sampling points.

steps.title: Regress dissimilarities against distance
steps.instruction: Perform linear regressions of each dissimilarity matrix against the geographic distance matrix; record the standardised regression coefficients as decay rates of similarity with distance.

steps.title: Mantel test of biotic vs geographic distance
steps.instruction: Correlate the biotic distance matrices with the geographic distance matrix using a Mantel test with 10 000 permutations (vegan R package).

steps.title: Decompose beta‑diversity components
steps.instruction: Using the ‘betapart’ R package, decompose (a) presence/absence dissimilarity into turnover (substitution) and nestedness components, and (b) abundance dissimilarity into balanced variation and abundance‑gradient components.

steps.title: Regress beta‑components on distance
steps.instruction: For each beta‑diversity component matrix, run linear regressions against the geographic distance matrix as described above to assess spatial relationships.
